social.title: Twenty-Five Taps at Weźże Krafta
social.description: A rotating wall of twenty-five Polish craft taps in a garden beside the Galicia Jewish Museum, with Neapolitan pizza to keep you upright.
social.bonus: Order only Polish breweries all night and find a stout worth writing down.

social.title: Bar-Hop the Old Tobacco Factory
social.description: Fifteen thousand square metres of 1870s cigarette factory at Dolnych Młynów 10, now thirty-odd bars, kitchens and studios around a courtyard the students never leave.
social.bonus: Have exactly one drink in four different places without repeating a style.

social.title: Cabaret at Piwnica pod Baranami
social.description: The legendary literary cabaret that ran underground through the communist decades, still performing in its original cellar on the Main Square with the same company of singers.
social.bonus: Stay to the end even though you won't catch every joke.

social.title: Find the Door at Mercy Brown
social.description: Kraków's original speakeasy: no sign, a hidden courtyard, a coat check and a flight of stairs, then a 1920s room with burlesque and live jazz and a bar on the world's top-500 list.
social.bonus: Find the entrance without looking up directions.

social.title: The Back Garden at Eszeweria
social.description: The most convincingly pre-war room in Kazimierz, chipped mirrors, oil lamps and sagging sofas, with a lilac-scented garden behind it in warm weather.
social.bonus: Sit in the garden until you lose track of what time it is.

social.title: Drinks in a Former Prayer House at Hevre
social.description: A nineteenth-century Kazimierz prayer house left deliberately unrestored, faded Hebrew murals and all, now serving unpasteurised tank Pilsner until four in the morning.
social.bonus: Find the surviving wall painting behind the bar and work out what it says.

social.title: A Hundred Vodkas at Wódka Cafe Bar
social.description: A single narrow room off Mały Rynek that has been pouring around a hundred flavoured vodkas since 2003, from chilli to Earl Grey to blackthorn.
social.bonus: Get a flight of four and rank them before anyone tells you what they were.

social.title: Three Floors of Techno at Prozak 2.0
social.description: A cellar club under Plac Domenikański with three dancefloors, four bars and a Funktion-One rig, running from ten at night until six in the morning.
social.bonus: Find all three dancefloors before you settle on one.

social.title: Sewing-Machine Tables at Singer
social.description: One of the first bars to open in Kazimierz, where the tables are antique Singer machines and you can still work the treadle with your feet while you drink.
social.bonus: Get the treadle going fast enough that someone asks you to stop.

social.title: Nightly Jazz at Harris Piano Jazz Bar
social.description: A brick cellar directly under the Main Square that puts on a live set every single night of the year, from standards to free improvisation.
social.bonus: Get a table close enough to the piano to watch the pianist's hands.

social.title: Candlelight and Jazz at Alchemia
social.description: The bar that made Kazimierz what it is: a warren of small rooms full of dripping candles and junk-shop furniture, with live music in the cellar most nights.
social.bonus: Find the smallest room in the place and claim it for the night.

social.title: Tank Beer at Stara Zajezdnia
social.description: A converted 1900s tram depot in Kazimierz holding the city's longest bar, its own microbrewery, and a deckchair garden out the back in summer.
social.bonus: Try all four house beers and pick the one the brewery should be known for.

chill.title: Finjan Coffee at Cheder
chill.description: A former Kazimierz prayer house run by the Jewish Culture Festival, where the coffee is brewed in a brass finjan and the shelves hold a lending library of Jewish history.
chill.bonus: Pull a book off the shelf and read a chapter before you leave.

chill.title: The Lilac Garden at Mleczarnia
chill.description: A walled Kazimierz courtyard garden across the street from the bar itself, all mismatched chairs under the trees, open from April until the weather turns.
chill.bonus: Order the hot beer with cloves at least once, ironically or not.

chill.title: An Afternoon Upstairs at Massolit
chill.description: An English-language bookshop in a set of old apartment rooms, with a café at the back, homemade cake, and armchairs nobody will move you out of.
chill.bonus: Leave with a book by a Polish author you'd never heard of.

chill.title: Glass Terrace Coffee at Bunkier
chill.description: A glassed-in conservatory jutting into the Planty gardens beside the modern art gallery, leafy in summer, sealed and warm in winter, good coffee all year.
chill.bonus: Take the seat closest to the glass and watch the park instead of your phone.

chill.title: Pour-Over at Karma Roasters
chill.description: Kraków's original specialty roastery on Krupnicza, pulling single origins on a Synesso and making its own kombucha and vegan cakes to go with them.
chill.bonus: Order the same bean as espresso and as filter and taste the difference back to back.

chill.title: Lap the Planty Ring
chill.description: Four kilometres of park laid out on the line of the demolished city walls, circling the entire Old Town under old chestnuts and limes.
chill.bonus: Walk the whole ring without cutting across the middle once.

chill.title: Art House Night at Kino Pod Baranami
chill.description: Three small screens inside a palace on the Main Square, showing European cinema in the original language and running festivals and all-night marathons.
chill.bonus: Pick the film with the title you understand least.

chill.title: Soak in the Chochołów Thermal Pools
chill.description: Poland's largest thermal complex, geothermal water pumped from three kilometres down into outdoor pools with the Tatra ridge line on the horizon.
chill.bonus: Sit in the outdoor pool until your hair freezes.

chill.title: Picnic on Bulwar Czerwieński
chill.description: The grassy Vistula embankment directly under Wawel, where half the city sits out on summer evenings with bread, cheese and a blanket while the river barges go past.
chill.bonus: Stay long enough that the castle floodlights come on above you.

chill.title: The Jagiellonian Botanical Garden
chill.description: Poland's oldest botanical garden, founded in 1783, with Victorian palm houses and a 200-year-old plane tree, ten minutes' walk east of the Old Town and almost always empty.
chill.bonus: Find the oldest tree in the garden and sit under it for ten minutes.

culture.title: Lady with an Ermine at the Czartoryski
culture.description: One of only around fifteen surviving Leonardo paintings, hanging in a rebuilt aristocratic palace museum, in its own room and worth the trip on its own.
culture.bonus: Stand with it for a full five minutes before you look at anything else.

culture.title: The State Rooms at Wawel
culture.description: The Polish kings' own castle on its limestone rock, with Flemish tapestries, the Crown Treasury, and a coffered ceiling studded with carved human heads.
culture.bonus: Count how many of the carved heads on the Envoys' Hall ceiling survive.

culture.title: Galicia Jewish Museum
culture.description: A Kazimierz warehouse hung with photographs of what is physically left of Jewish Galicia, overgrown cemeteries and converted synagogues, rather than another chronology of the war.
culture.bonus: Pick the one photograph you'd want to go and stand in front of yourself.

culture.title: Auschwitz-Birkenau Memorial
culture.description: An hour and a half west of Kraków, the preserved camps and the state museum built inside them: the single most important thing you can do from this city, and the hardest.
culture.bonus: Book the extended study tour rather than the standard one, and don't rush Birkenau.

culture.title: The Hejnał from St Mary's Tower
culture.description: A trumpeter has played the hejnał from the taller tower every hour for centuries, always breaking off mid-note; inside is Veit Stoss's vast carved altarpiece.
culture.bonus: Be standing in the square on the hour and spot which window the trumpet comes from.

culture.title: Schindler's Factory
culture.description: The enamel works itself, turned into an immersive museum of Kraków under occupation, reconstructed tram carriages, ghetto streets and Schindler's actual office.
culture.bonus: Walk from here to the surviving fragment of the ghetto wall afterwards.

culture.title: Rynek Underground
culture.description: Four metres below the Main Square, the excavated medieval market laid out exactly as it was found, with holograms of traders projected into the old streets.
culture.bonus: Find the medieval road surface and stand on the original cobbles.

culture.title: MOCAK Contemporary Art
culture.description: A purpose-built contemporary art museum in the old factory yard next to Schindler's, deliberately programmed as the argumentative counterweight to Kraków's heritage.
culture.bonus: Find one piece you actively dislike and work out why.

8ball.title: Wildcard: Plac Nowy Until the Window Closes
8ball.description: Start at any bar on Plac Nowy, move one door along every time you finish a drink, and don't stop until you're back at the zapiekanka window at closing time.
8ball.bonus: Talk to someone new at every single stop.

8ball.title: Wildcard: Milk Bar Roulette
8ball.description: Walk into any bar mleczny, order the third thing on the board whatever it is, and eat the whole thing before you look up what you just had.
8ball.bonus: Do it in two different milk bars in one afternoon.

foodie.title: Pierogi Flight at Przystanek Pierogarnia
foodie.description: Hand-pinched dumplings sold by the half-portion, so you can work through ruskie, lentil-and-carrot and the sweet ones in a single sitting.
foodie.bonus: Order one filling you can't translate.

foodie.title: Morning Haul at Stary Kleparz
foodie.description: Six hundred years of continuous trading just outside the old walls: smoked oscypek, sour cream by the tub, forest mushrooms in season and no gift shops.
foodie.bonus: Buy something you can't identify and ask the seller how to cook it.

foodie.title: Hummus Breakfast at Hamsa
foodie.description: Israeli breakfast on Szeroka Street, straight across from the old synagogues: warm hummus, shakshuka and far too much pita, from nine in the morning.
foodie.bonus: Finish the bowl using only bread, no cutlery.

foodie.title: Shape Your Own Obwarzanek
foodie.description: An hour in a working bakery museum learning to plait and boil the braided ring bread that has been sold from Kraków street carts for centuries and now carries EU protected status.
foodie.bonus: Plait yours tightly enough that it survives the boiling without unravelling.

foodie.title: House-Infused Vodka at Starka
foodie.description: Interwar Kazimierz recreated in one room: slow-cooked duck, potato pancakes, and a row of the restaurant's own infusions in unlabelled bottles behind the bar.
foodie.bonus: Let the waiter pick your infusion instead of reading the list.

foodie.title: Milk-Bar Lunch at Pod Temidą
foodie.description: A surviving communist-era canteen on Grodzka where a full plate of żurek, pierogi and fruit compote still costs less than a cocktail.
foodie.bonus: Order entirely by pointing at the board, no English.

foodie.title: Zapiekanka at Endzior
foodie.description: Half a metre of open-faced baguette loaded with mushrooms and cheese, handed over the counter of the round market hall on Plac Nowy until two in the morning.
foodie.bonus: Order it with the full complement of sauces and eat it standing up.

foodie.title: Two Michelin Stars at Bottiglieria 1881
foodie.description: Twenty seats in a Kazimierz cellar and the only two-star kitchen in Poland, where Przemysław Klima rebuilds Polish dishes from the ground up, course by course.
foodie.bonus: Take the wine pairing and let the sommelier choose blind for one course.

foodie.title: Cheesecake at Cafe Camelot
foodie.description: A low-ceilinged Old Town room full of folk carvings and candle stubs, serving the best sernik in the centre to people who have clearly been coming for twenty years.
foodie.bonus: Stay for a second pot of tea and finish whatever you're reading.

foodie.title: Vegan Sushi at Youmiko
foodie.description: A tiny Kazimierz counter doing fish-free nigiri that has no business being this good: fermented vegetables, smoked tofu, and a tasting set built in front of you.
foodie.bonus: Take the tasting menu and eat every piece in the order it's handed to you.

foodie.title: Pork Knuckle and a Litre at Pod Wawelem
foodie.description: A vast beer hall at the foot of Wawel where the portions are deliberately absurd and the standard measure is a litre in a handled mug.
foodie.bonus: Split one knuckle three ways and admit you still couldn't finish it.

foodie.title: Highlander Dinner at Morskie Oko
foodie.description: An art nouveau house on Plac Szczepański fitted out as a Tatra lodge, with open fires, grilled sheep's cheese and a live highland band that does not do quiet.
foodie.bonus: Stay for the moment the band tries to get the whole room singing.

adventure.title: Climb the Twardowski Rocks
adventure.description: Bolted limestone walls rising straight out of the Zakrzówek park, the crag where generations of Polish alpinists learned to climb, ten minutes from Kazimierz.
adventure.bonus: Lead a route, however easy, instead of only seconding.

adventure.title: 135 Metres Down in the Wieliczka Salt Mine
adventure.description: Seven centuries of tunnels cut through rock salt, including a full underground cathedral with chandeliers and altarpieces carved from the walls themselves.
adventure.bonus: Lick the wall once, discreetly, to confirm it really is salt.

adventure.title: Trail of the Eagles' Nests to Rabsztyn
adventure.description: A stretch of the medieval castle trail across the Jura's white rock outcrops, ending at a hilltop ruin rebuilt just enough to climb.
adventure.bonus: Get to the top of the keep and pick out the next castle along the ridge line.

adventure.title: Whitewater on the Kolna Slalom Course
adventure.description: A 320-metre artificial whitewater channel on the edge of the city where Olympic slalom paddlers train, open to anyone willing to take an instructor and get soaked.
adventure.bonus: Run the course a second time without capsizing.

adventure.title: Slides and Saunas at Park Wodny
adventure.description: Poland's original big aquapark: eight hundred metres of slides, a wild river and a serious saunarium, which is exactly what a grey Kraków afternoon calls for.
adventure.bonus: Take the fastest slide first, before you have time to think about it.

adventure.title: Raft the Dunajec Gorge
adventure.description: Eighteen kilometres through the Pieniny limestone gorge on lashed-together wooden rafts, punted by highlanders in embroidered waistcoats who have run this river for generations.
adventure.bonus: Get your raftsman to tell you which cliff has the legend attached.

adventure.title: Sunset on the Kościuszko Mound
adventure.description: A spiral path up a 34-metre earthwork raised by hand in the 1820s, ending on a ring wall with the whole city on one side and the Tatras on the other.
adventure.bonus: Pick out both the Wawel roof and the steelworks chimneys from the same spot.

adventure.title: Nowa Huta in a Trabant
adventure.description: Kraków's Stalinist steel-town district toured in a two-stroke Trabant, with stops at a shop kept in 1950s trim and a workers' canteen that never changed.
adventure.bonus: Take the wheel long enough to stall it at least once.

adventure.title: Swim the Zakrzówek Quarry Lagoon
adventure.description: Turquoise water in a flooded limestone quarry ringed by white cliffs, with lifeguarded floating pools that only open for about eleven weeks a year.
adventure.bonus: Get there early enough to beat the 300-person daily cap.

adventure.title: Walk Dolina Kościeliska
adventure.description: The gentlest of the great Tatra valleys: a flat limestone trough between vertical walls, with a cave partway up and a shepherds' hut serving sour milk at the top.
adventure.bonus: Take the side path up to the Mroźna cave and go in.

adventure.title: Cycle the Vistula to Tyniec Abbey
adventure.description: Twelve flat kilometres of riverside path out of the city to an eleventh-century Benedictine abbey standing on a white limestone bluff above the water.
adventure.bonus: Buy the monks' bread at the abbey shop and eat it on the bluff.

adventure.title: Ride Las Wolski to the Piłsudski Mound
adventure.description: A proper climb on gravel forest roads through the city's big western woodland to the tallest of Kraków's four memorial mounds.
adventure.bonus: Make it to the top without putting a foot down.

adventure.title: Beach Day at Bagry Lagoon
adventure.description: A former gravel pit turned city swimming lake fifteen minutes from the Old Town, with a sand beach, a sailing club and almost no tourists.
adventure.bonus: Swim out to the far buoy line and back.

adventure.title: Cable Car up Kasprowy Wierch
adventure.description: A 1936 cableway out of Zakopane that lifts you to a 1,987-metre summit straddling the Slovak border, where the ridge walks start straight off the platform.
adventure.bonus: Walk at least as far as the next saddle rather than turning round at the café.

adventure.title: Ojców Valley to Pieskowa Skała
adventure.description: Poland's smallest national park: a limestone gorge full of caves and freestanding rock pillars, walked end to end to a Renaissance castle perched on a cliff.
adventure.bonus: Find the Hercules' Club pillar and get a photo where it looks about to topple.

adventure.title: Morskie Oko Before the Crowds
adventure.description: The Tatras' most famous lake, a black glacial eye under 2,000-metre walls, worth the pre-dawn start from Kraków to walk the access road in the cold and briefly have it to yourself.
adventure.bonus: Carry on up to Czarny Staw above it while everyone else stops at the hut.
